description.value: The study investigated longitudinal white matter changes in frontotemporal dementia subtypes using diffusion tensor imaging and compared them with regional grey matter atrophy over 12 months.
A longitudinal observational study compared three frontotemporal dementia subtypes with age- and sex-matched healthy controls at baseline and 12 months.

name.value: Longitudinal white matter changes in bvFTD

spans.text: TBSS results of longitudinal white matter changes in bvFTD.

definition.value: Longitudinal changes in FA from baseline to 12 months in bvFTD

value: At 12 months, extensive bilateral changes continued in most white matter tracts across all DTI metrics compared to baseline measurements, with additional involvement of the splenium of the corpus callosum. Longitudinal changes in FA and RadialD were concordant and showed the most extensive changes among all metrics.

name.value: Longitudinal white matter changes in PNFA

spans.text: TBSS results of longitudinal white matter changes in PNFA.

definition.value: Longitudinal changes in FA from baseline to 12 months in PNFA

value: After 12 months, additional white matter abnormalities were observed in the anterior thalamic radiation, anterior cingulum, uncinate fasciculus, genu of the corpus callosum, and brainstem, with changes becoming more pronounced in the right compared to the left hemisphere. Longitudinal DTI changes were observed in FA, MD, and RadialD only.

name.value: Longitudinal white matter changes in SD

spans.text: TBSS results of longitudinal white matter changes in SD.

definition.value: Longitudinal changes in FA from baseline to 12 months in SD

value: Progressive longitudinal white matter changes in the SD group extended into frontal and commissural tracts at 12 months, with less progression in left temporal regions. Longitudinal alterations in FA were most extensive compared to the other metrics in SD, particularly in frontal white matter regions.
